note: v3 fix round (fix3-econ): the fiscal levers. Gameplay rules in scripts/sim/sim_economy.gd (see API.md, 'v3 fix round (fix3-econ)'). Amounts are game units: 'gold_quarters' is a multiple of the average quarterly income, 'upkeep_pct' a lasting change to all upkeep (buildings, districts, public services, units), 'years' how long a lasting term runs. Each lever names who argued for it at the time (advocate) and the year history used it (historical); a cite quotes the opened page verbatim. Gameplay thresholds, not historical claims.

structural.note: The structural-deficit alarm (v3 final round, fix4-econ): every recurring outflow (running costs, readiness, absorption, policy cards, negative lasting terms and rails, event costs, food imports, debt service) above 110% of gross revenue (taxes plus every positive transfer) for four quarters in a row, or above history's own ratio at that date plus 20 points when history ran a deeper deficit (1949-52); it clears after two quarters at or below 100% (or history's ratio).

mothball.note: A mothballed building keeps 20% of its upkeep (guarding, basic maintenance) and gives nothing until it is reopened for six quarters of its upkeep (times the era's gold scale). Closing it ends the upkeep for good; a closed service building (amenities, housing or trust) costs that city's Civic Trust. A mothball plan (v3 final round) takes at most two buildings, and at most one that serves residents, from any one city, and never takes a city below zero amenities or short of housing.

privatisations.name: Sell the state's holdings in banks and investment companies
privatisations.desc: Minority stakes inherited from the Yishuv and the first years of the state go to private buyers: one-off revenue, and the budget no longer carries their losses.
privatisations.advocate: The General Zionists (private initiative over state economic controls)

cite.claim: State companies were sold from the 1960s: 64 between 1962 and 1977
The General Zionists' 1952 coalition terms called for scrapping state economic controls
cite.quote: Economic controls shall be scrapped, except on materials which cannot be produced in the country.

privatisations.name: Sell government companies to private investors (the 1978 decision)
privatisations.desc: A ministerial committee lists dozens of government companies for sale: a larger one-off sum and lower subsidies, against the unions' opposition.
privatisations.advocate: Finance Minister Simcha Ehrlich (Likud), the 1977 economic liberalisation

cite.claim: On 5 March 1978 the ministerial committee decided to sell 47 companies
cite.quote: ב-5 במרץ 1978 החליטה ועדת שרים לענייני כלכלה על מכירת 47 חברות כדי לצמצם את מעורבות הממשלה במשק הישראלי
המהפך הכלכלי הוא השם שניתן לתוכנית הליברליזציה הכלכלית שהציג שר האוצר שמחה ארליך ב-29 באוקטובר 1977

privatisations.name: A privatisation programme for the large state firms
privatisations.desc: Shares of the big state-owned firms are floated or sold in blocks: steady revenue and leaner firms, as Britain was doing at the time.
privatisations.advocate: The Finance Ministry after the 1985 stabilisation (market-oriented structural reforms)

cite.quote: The privatization processes in Israel intensified in 1986 following the intensified privatization in Britain in the 1980s.

privatisations.name: Sell Bezeq, Israel Chemicals and ZIM
privatisations.desc: The telephone company, the chemicals group and the national shipping line are sold: a large sum, but the Bezeq workers and the Histadrut strike over pensions and jobs.
privatisations.hist_label: 1997: 13 state firms put up for sale
privatisations.advocate: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government (sale of 13 state firms)

cite.claim: The 1997 plan to sell 13 state firms, including Bezeq, Israel Chemicals and ZIM
cite.quote: some 13 state firms, including the Bezek telephone company, Israel Chemicals and Zim shipping would be sold by the end of 1997

cite.claim: Bezeq workers struck over the sale
cite.quote: Bezek workers demanded that proceeds from the sale go to implementing wage, severance and pensions agreements with the government.

privatisations.name: Sell the banks nationalised in 1983
privatisations.desc: The controlling stakes the state took in the bank-shares crisis are sold to private groups.
privatisations.advocate: The Finance Ministry (the 1997 sale of Bank Hapoalim to the Arison group)

cite.claim: In 1997 a private group bought 43% of Bank Hapoalim
cite.quote: has acquired a 43 percent stake in Bank Hapoalim

privatisations.name: Float El Al and the remaining large state firms
privatisations.desc: The national airline and other large state firms are floated on the stock exchange.
privatisations.advocate: The Government Companies Authority's privatisation programme

cite.claim: El Al is among the companies privatised

versions.name: Austerity with compulsory savings
versions.desc: Rationing, compulsory savings and deep cuts in state spending stop the printing of money: prices steady, but wages and services are squeezed.
versions.advocate: Dov Yosef, Minister of Rationing and Supply (the 1949 austerity programme)

cite.claim: The 1949 austerity programme with compulsory saving
cite.quote: Dr. Dov Joseph, Minister of Food and Supply, told representatives of the press that the monthly consumption of food under the new austerity diet will cost about six pounds

versions.name: A new economic policy: devalue, freeze wages and cut the budget
versions.desc: A devaluation, a wage and price freeze with lower cost-of-living allowances, compulsory savings and spending cuts, as in 1962 and in Sapir's 1966 plan: unemployment rises for a while.
versions.advocate: Finance Ministers Levi Eshkol (1962) and Pinhas Sapir (1966)

cite.claim: The Knesset backed the 1962 new economic policy
cite.quote: Knesset (Parliament) today voted support of the Governments new economic policy

cite.claim: Sapir's 1966 economic plan: wage and price freeze, lower allowances
cite.quote: Mr. Sapir has been the principal architect of the new economic plan which was adopted by the Cabinet last night

cite.claim: Mapam opposed it as too hard on wage earners
cite.quote: Mapam holds that the Sapir plan bears too heavily on the wage earners.

versions.name: An emergency stabilisation plan (budget cuts, wage freeze, fixed exchange rate)
versions.desc: The 1985 model: deep budget cuts, a wage agreement with the Histadrut, temporary price controls, a devaluation and then a fixed exchange rate, and no more printing of money for the deficit.
versions.advocate: Finance Minister Yitzhak Moda'i and the economist Michael Bruno (July 1985)

cite.claim: The 1985 plan was devised by Moda'i and Bruno
cite.quote: The plan was devised by Yitzhak Moda'i and Michael Bruno.

cite.claim: It ended central-bank financing of the deficit
cite.quote: Curbing the Bank of Israel's ability to print money to cover government deficits.

readiness.note: v3 final round (fix4-econ, item 2): holding the forces at high readiness costs gold (training, reserve duty and munitions stocks): nothing up to Readiness 60, then up to 6% of the average quarterly income at 100. Readiness decays by 2 points a quarter (to at most 20) while the treasury stays below zero beyond history's own overdraft, and recovers by 4 a quarter once it is paid again. Above 80 every further point is dearer (80 + 20 x (1 - e^(-(raw - 80) / 20))). Gameplay rules, not historical claims.

policy_cuts.note: v3 final round (fix4-econ, N1): scale back (half strength: half the card's cost and half its benefits) or suspend (the card keeps its slot and does nothing) a slotted policy card that costs gold (Social Security, Universal Health Coverage, the Absorption Basket, MASHAV aid, the housing lottery). History's own cuts are the model: the 1985 stabilisation plan's cut in government spending and the 2002-03 cuts in allowances and social services. Restoring is free; taking the card out of its slot ends the cut.

versions.name: Cut the card's spending, as in the 1985 plan
versions.hist_label: 1985: a deep cut in government spending (the stabilisation plan)
versions.desc: Benefit rates and the services the card pays for are cut, as the 1985 stabilisation plan cut government spending: the budget gains at once, and the people who rely on them lose.
versions.advocate: Finance Minister Yitzhak Moda'i and the economist Michael Bruno (the 1985 plan's cut in government expenditure)

cite.claim: The 1985 stabilisation plan made a significant cut in government expenditure
cite.quote: A significant cut in government expenditures and deficit.

cite.claim: The plan was devised by Moda'i and Bruno
cite.quote: The plan was devised by Yitzhak Moda'i and Michael Bruno.

versions.name: Cut the card's spending, as in the 2002-03 budgets
versions.hist_label: 2002-03: cuts in allowances and social services, welfare to work
versions.desc: Allowances and the services the card pays for are cut, as the 2002 and 2003 budgets cut social services and Netanyahu's recovery plan tied welfare to work: the budget gains at once, and the people who rely on them lose.
versions.advocate: Finance Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (the 2003 economic recovery plan: welfare to work, a three-year spending freeze)

cite.claim: The 2003 plan tied welfare to work and froze government spending
cite.quote: He instituted a program to end welfare dependency by requiring people to apply for jobs or training, reduced the size of the public sector, froze government spending for three years
Cuts in social services and education also are expected, likely drawing howls of protests from politicians representing the weaker sectors of society.
